audit.post_reveal_observations: The Graham Hill portrait visibly shows a moustache. Original/native Mustache are semantically correct but score zero; support changes to beard, a visual deterioration hidden by the tied score. It deletes R013 (119 tokens) and retains the bearded Wes Johnson portrait R038 (187). QTP removes 2,481 tokens upstream.
audit.counterevidence: The successful scored likelihood objective does not ensure the generated answer matches gold; wrong-person competition is plausible but the other retained text and prefix states remain uncontrolled.

audit.proposed_followup: Add R013 to the support set versus a 119-token comparable portrait/control addition; separately remove R038 from full context and use a matched-budget swap. Score moustache and beard explicitly, keeping original gold scores unchanged in historical results.

selected_case_evidence.question: What ancient kingdom built several temples to the Egyptian god Amun in what is now Sudan and South Sudan?

audit.post_reveal_observations: All arms answer Kush (.5) against Kingdom of Kush. Rank-1 Kawa text R015 (298) names Taharqa/other kings of Kush, while rank-2 architecture text R021 (280) provides overlapping support. Support removes the map R019 (254).
audit.counterevidence: Kush is a semantically valid short form. Egyptian pharaohs in the same passage are also real builders, so treating every alternative kingdom name as a false distractor would misread the document.
audit.missing_evidence: Separate necessity of Kawa and architecture support; answer-alias adjudication.
audit.proposed_followup: Test R015 and R021 individually and jointly removed, with controls matching their different costs; hold qualifiers/captions fixed. This can distinguish redundancy from complementary localization.
